title: HO2S Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 / Bank 2 Sensor 1
shortDescription: The PCM detected that upstream oxygen sensor signals between Bank 1 and Bank 2 appear to be reversed.
fullDescription:
Code P0040 sets when the PCM's rationality test determines that the upstream HO2S on Bank 1 is responding to conditions that match Bank 2, and vice versa. This typically happens after sensor replacement where connectors were swapped.

The result is improper fuel trim responses, since the PCM is adjusting fuel to the wrong bank. Symptoms frequently include poor fuel economy, a rough idle, and possible misfire codes appearing together.

Diagnosis focuses on verifying wiring routing from each sensor to its PCM pin. A wiring swap during repair is the single most common root cause.
safetyImpact: Increased emissions and reduced drivability, but not an immediate safety hazard.

causes.cause: Upstream HO2S connectors swapped between banks
Wiring harness modification or repair error

symptoms: Fuel trim codes on one bank

fixSteps.title: Scan and document
fixSteps.instruction: Record live data from both upstream O2 sensors during warm idle.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor routing
fixSteps.instruction: Trace harness from each upstream sensor to the PCM connector and confirm pin assignments.

fixSteps.title: Swap connectors to correct banks
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect the sensors to their proper bank harness plugs.

fixSteps.title: Clear code and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Clear DTCs and drive through a complete OBD monitor cycle.

faq.a: Short term yes, but fuel economy and emissions will suffer.
Usually no — most cases are wiring swap after a recent repair.

title: HO2S Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 2 / Bank 2 Sensor 2
shortDescription: Downstream oxygen sensor signals appear reversed between banks.
fullDescription:
P0041 sets when the downstream (post-catalyst) O2 sensors return signals that correlate with the opposite bank. This commonly happens after catalytic converter or sensor replacement.

Because the downstream sensors are used for catalyst monitoring, swapped signals can trigger false catalyst efficiency codes. The PCM sees mismatched transitions when comparing upstream to downstream.

Correction requires verifying the post-cat harness routing and pin assignments at the PCM.
safetyImpact: No direct safety impact; emissions compliance affected.

causes.cause: Damaged wiring clip holding sensors to wrong side

fixSteps.title: Read live data
fixSteps.instruction: Observe both downstream sensors during steady cruise.

fixSteps.title: Inspect routing
fixSteps.instruction: Follow each post-cat harness back to its PCM pin.

fixSteps.title: Correct connections
fixSteps.instruction: Reattach sensors to their correct bank plugs.

faq.a: No, but unresolved fuel trim issues from related codes could.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater control circuit fault on the third O2 sensor of Bank 1.
fullDescription:
P0042 applies to vehicles with three oxygen sensors per bank, typical on diesel particulate filter-equipped and some late-model gasoline applications. The heater on Sensor 3 is not responding as expected to PCM control pulses.

Without proper heater operation, the sensor takes too long to reach operating temperature and closed-loop monitoring is delayed. This affects emissions readiness monitors.

Fault isolation involves checking the heater power feed, PCM-side ground control, and the sensor's internal heater resistance.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; emissions monitors may not complete.

fixSteps.title: Check heater fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the fuse feeding the O2 heater circuit for this bank.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance across the sensor heater pins; compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if open
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the O2 sensor if the heater reads open or out of range.

faq.a: The car will run but emissions tests may fail.

title: HO2S Short Term Fuel Trim Sensor Lean Bank 1 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Sensor 3 on Bank 1 is reporting persistent lean STFT conditions.
fullDescription:
P0043 sets when the PCM cannot maintain stoichiometric fuel trim using Sensor 3 feedback on Bank 1. The STFT correction stays pegged toward the lean side for an extended time.

Unlike upstream lean codes, Sensor 3 is typically after a secondary catalyst or at the DPF outlet; a lean reading here may reflect true exhaust gas composition or sensor aging.

Diagnosis includes verifying sensor bias voltage, exhaust leak checks near the sensor, and comparing live data to the upstream sensor.
safetyImpact: Emissions and mileage impact; no immediate safety risk.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Pressure-test or smoke-test the exhaust between cat and sensor.

fixSteps.title: Compare sensor data
fixSteps.instruction: Log Sensor 1 and Sensor 3 voltages at varying loads.

faq.q: Is exhaust leak the most common cause?
faq.a: Yes, it's frequently a small leak near the sensor bung.

title: HO2S Short Term Fuel Trim Sensor Rich Bank 1 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Persistent rich STFT at Bank 1 Sensor 3.
fullDescription:
This code sets when the downstream STFT sensor shows extended rich bias. Excess hydrocarbons past the cat suggest either a real overly rich mixture, a saturated converter, or a contaminated sensor.

PCM response is limited to flagging the condition rather than adjusting fuel, because primary trim is driven by upstream sensors. However, monitor completion is affected.

Repair order: scan for companion codes, check for oil/coolant consumption, then inspect the sensor itself.
safetyImpact: None directly; indirect damage possible to catalyst.

fixSteps.title: Check companion codes
fixSteps.instruction: Address any upstream fuel trim codes first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Look for coolant or oil entering combustion.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if contaminated
fixSteps.instruction: Install new OEM sensor after resolving the root cause.

faq.a: Yes, prolonged rich conditions overheat and contaminate cats.

title: Turbo/Super Charger Boost Control Solenoid Circuit
shortDescription: An electrical fault is detected in the boost control solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
P0045 is set when the PCM detects the boost control solenoid command and feedback are inconsistent, indicating an open, short, or high resistance in the circuit.

The solenoid controls wastegate pressure or VGT actuation; without it, boost will default to mechanical limits, often meaning low or unregulated boost.

Diagnosis proceeds from scan data to wiring checks at the solenoid connector, then solenoid resistance versus spec.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; could limit safe merging acceleration.

causes.cause: Open or shorted wiring to solenoid

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check the solenoid connector for corrosion or bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Measure solenoid resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare reading to service manual specification.

fixSteps.title: Replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the solenoid or repair wiring based on findings.

faq.q: Will the car enter limp mode?
faq.a: Often yes, to protect the turbo from overboost.

title: Turbo/Super Charger Boost Control Solenoid B Circuit High
shortDescription: Voltage on the B-circuit of the boost solenoid is higher than expected.
fullDescription:
Code P0048 sets when the PCM measures voltage above the upper threshold on the B-side boost solenoid control. This commonly stems from an open control ground or an internally open solenoid.

On twin-turbo or VGT systems this fault may only affect one turbocharger, producing asymmetric boost.

Tests target the PCM ground path, the solenoid itself, and the harness between them.
safetyImpact: Possible reduced power and limp mode.

causes.cause: Loss of ground to PCM driver

fixSteps.title: Check control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm continuity from solenoid connector to PCM pin.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify solenoid resistance is within spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid or repair harness based on results.

faq.q: Twin turbo — do both sides fail?
faq.a: No, the B circuit usually affects only one side.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1 Advanced Diag
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic path for Bank 2 Sensor 1 heater circuit fault.
fullDescription:
The PCM reports an electrical abnormality in the heater control circuit of the upstream O2 sensor on Bank 2. The advanced path applies when standard circuit tests pass but the fault persists during drive cycles.

Intermittent faults often trace to chafed harness segments near heat shields, or to connector moisture ingress.

Use scope capture during cold start to catch intermittent opens.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing along exhaust routing.

fixSteps.title: Scope capture
fixSteps.instruction: Capture heater PWM during cold start.

faq.a: Scope the heater line and flex harness while watching for dropouts.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 2 Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for heater resistance outside spec on Bank 2 Sensor 2.
fullDescription:
Code P0060 sets when the PCM calculates heater resistance out of specification on the downstream O2 sensor of Bank 2. Aging heaters drift high over time.

The advanced approach adds measuring amperage during warm-up and comparing to the companion bank.

Replacement of the sensor usually resolves the issue; confirm harness voltage drop first.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; emissions readiness delayed.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater amperage
fixSteps.instruction: Use a low-amp clamp during cold start.

faq.a: Slightly; cold temps exaggerate drift.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater resistance out of range on Bank 2 Sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0061 indicates the PCM has measured the heater circuit resistance of the Bank 2, Sensor 3 sensor outside the calibrated window. This sensor is usually downstream of the second catalyst on V-engines.

A reading that creeps higher over time is typical of a sensor nearing end of life. An abrupt change often signals a wiring issue.

Repair focuses on confirming the resistance measurement at the sensor pins before replacement.

fixSteps.title: Measure at pins
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance at the sensor heater pins.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or replace if pins corroded.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit OEM sensor if out of spec.

faq.a: No — internal heater element cannot be serviced.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Electrical fault in heater control circuit for Bank 2 Sensor 3.
fullDescription:
The PCM cannot command the heater on Bank 2 Sensor 3 as expected. This typically presents as an open in the PCM-side driver ground path or an open heater element.

Symptoms are minimal other than a MIL and readiness delays. Long-term, the sensor cannot support closed-loop catalyst monitoring reliably.

Diagnosis follows the standard heater fault flow.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the O2 heater fuse is good.

fixSteps.title: Circuit test
fixSteps.instruction: Check power and ground at sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor if element open.

faq.a: 30-60 minutes for a typical wiring/fuse check.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Low voltage on the heater control circuit for Bank 2 Sensor 3.
fullDescription:
The PCM measures control voltage below threshold, implying a short to ground or a stuck-on driver. Left unresolved, the heater may run continuously and shorten sensor life.

Because this is a downstream sensor, drivability impact is limited; however, readiness monitors will not complete.

Locate the short with a voltage drop test along the control wire.

causes.cause: Short to ground in control wire

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check if short persists with sensor unplugged.

fixSteps.title: Trace control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for pinch points and abrasions.

fixSteps.title: Repair short
fixSteps.instruction: Splice damaged wire or replace sensor.

faq.a: Possible, but shorts usually protect the driver first.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: High voltage measured on Bank 2 Sensor 3 heater control circuit.
fullDescription:
Code P0064 appears when the heater control sees voltage above spec with no response to the PCM's PWM duty cycle. Typical causes are open circuit conditions or a failed ground path.

Diagnosis favors checking for physical wire break near the sensor's flex service loop.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity from sensor ground to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Inspect service loop
fixSteps.instruction: Look for broken wires near heat shield.

fixSteps.title: Splice repair
fixSteps.instruction: Repair break and protect with heat shrink.

faq.a: Yes — vibration can reopen a marginal break.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
shortDescription: Air assist performance outside expected range.
fullDescription:
Code P0065 sets when the PCM detects the air assist control does not follow the commanded setpoint during injector atomization events. Primarily seen on legacy systems with auxiliary air injection.

Reduced atomization leads to rough idle and elevated HC emissions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for click and check for plugged ports.

fixSteps.title: Service or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or replace solenoid as needed.

faq.a: Select early 2000s Toyota and Honda models.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on air assisted injector control circuit.
fullDescription: P0066 indicates the control circuit of the air assisted injector system is reading below the expected threshold. Often due to a short to ground or open driver pull-up.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Trace wire from solenoid to PCM for shorts.

faq.a: Wire abrasion near intake manifold bolts.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on air assisted injector control circuit.
fullDescription: The air assist control wire measures above spec. Often because the solenoid has an open coil or the control wire is disconnected.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Install new unit if coil open.

faq.a: Usually only cold-start rough idle.

title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation Advanced
shortDescription: Correlation between MAP/MAF and throttle position is out of range.
fullDescription:
Advanced variant of P0068 that sets when rationality checks between the throttle position sensor and the MAP or MAF readings disagree during transient throttle changes.

Common triggers include vacuum leaks, a restricted air filter, a contaminated MAF, or a sticking throttle body.

Diagnosis focuses on comparing idle and WOT values against the service manual tables.
safetyImpact: Potential unexpected acceleration feel; powertrain may enter reduced power mode.

faq.a: Cleaning is a quick first step; check for vacuum leaks too.

title: MAP - Barometric Pressure Correlation
shortDescription: Correlation between MAP and barometric pressure sensors is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0069 sets when the PCM finds the key-on MAP reading inconsistent with the ambient baro reading, or with stored baro learned at startup.

This often indicates a stuck or biased MAP sensor or a vacuum leak allowing ambient air to influence MAP readings.

fixSteps.title: Compare KOEO readings
fixSteps.instruction: MAP and baro should be within 3 kPa at key-on.

fixSteps.title: Replace MAP
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor if out of spec.

faq.a: Yes — baro changes with altitude; sensor must track it.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Ambient air temperature sensor reading outside expected range.
fullDescription:
P0070 indicates the PCM-monitored ambient temp sensor reads outside a reasonable envelope compared to intake air temp at key-on.

A large delta between IAT and AAT after a long soak points to sensor drift or wiring issues.

The ambient sensor also feeds HVAC and compressor strategy, so A/C operation may be affected.

fixSteps.title: Compare sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Key-on cold, compare IAT and AAT.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check for bug damage or corrosion.

faq.a: Typically behind the front grille.

title: System Voltage Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic path for abnormal system voltage detected by the PCM.
fullDescription:
P0560 represents a non-specific voltage fault and is often accompanied by more specific voltage codes. Causes range from a weak battery, failing alternator, to a corroded main ground.

The advanced path captures keyed-up, cranking, and post-start voltages to isolate the failing element.
safetyImpact: Unexpected stalling possible if voltage drops far enough.

fixSteps.title: Inspect grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Clean and torque main ground straps.

faq.a: Yes — most cases start with a weak battery.

title: System Voltage Unstable Advanced
shortDescription: System voltage is fluctuating outside limits.
fullDescription:
P0561 appears when the PCM sees voltage bouncing between high and low values. Most often it's a loose battery terminal, a failing alternator diode, or a cracked alternator wire.

Unstable voltage can trigger secondary codes in sensors and modules across the vehicle.

fixSteps.title: Torque cables
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm battery terminals tight and clean.

fixSteps.title: AC ripple test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure AC voltage on battery while running.

faq.q: How much AC ripple is too much?
faq.a: Above ~0.1V AC suggests a bad diode.

title: System Voltage Low Advanced
shortDescription: System voltage below threshold while running.
fullDescription: P0562 advanced variant sets when voltage drops below ~10.5V engine running. The most common cause is a failed alternator or broken drive belt.
safetyImpact: Engine may stall; loss of power steering assist on failure.

faq.a: Briefly, but stalling risk rises as battery depletes.

title: System Voltage High Advanced
shortDescription: System voltage above threshold.
fullDescription:
Advanced P0563 presents when running voltage exceeds ~16V. Causes include a failed voltage regulator, damaged alternator, or wiring fault causing overcharging.

Prolonged overcharging shortens battery life and may damage electronic modules.
safetyImpact: Possible module damage, battery swelling, fire risk in severe cases.

fixSteps.title: Check sense wire
fixSteps.instruction: Verify integrity of sense lead to regulator.

faq.a: Yes — risk of module damage. Stop driving.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Signal
shortDescription: Signal from cruise control multi-function input A is invalid.
fullDescription: P0564 sets when the cruise multi-function switch input is out of range. Typical causes are resistive ladder drift, corroded clock spring contacts, or a failed cruise switch.

faq.a: Yes, but no cruise.

title: Cruise Control On Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise control On signal not detected.
fullDescription: P0565 sets when the cruise On signal is missing or stuck. The PCM cannot arm cruise without this signal; cruise remains disabled.

faq.a: Without it cruise will not engage.

title: Cruise Control Off Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise control Off signal invalid.
fullDescription: Advanced P0566 applies when the PCM cannot reliably read the cruise Off signal, preventing proper disable logic.

faq.a: Avoid using it until repaired.

title: Cruise Control Resume Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise control Resume signal invalid.
fullDescription: The PCM does not see a proper Resume button signal. Commonly due to a worn rubber contact in the steering wheel switch.

faq.a: Yes.

title: Cruise Control Set Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise Set signal invalid.
fullDescription: Similar to P0567 but affects the Set button signal. Cruise cannot be set; wiring and switch are primary suspects.

faq.a: No — without Set, cruise is unusable.

title: Cruise Control Coast Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise Coast signal invalid.
fullDescription: P0569 sets when the Coast/Decel signal is missing or stuck. This prevents cruise from decelerating on demand.

faq.a: Minor; coast can be done with brakes.

title: Cruise Control Accel Signal Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise Accel signal invalid.
fullDescription: P0570 sets when the Accel signal is invalid or missing, preventing cruise speed increase commands.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Verify clean contact on Accel press.

faq.a: Yes; accel just not available.

title: Cruise Control / Brake Switch A Signal Advanced
shortDescription: Cruise/brake A-switch signal invalid.
fullDescription:
P0571 appears when the Brake Switch A input used by cruise is abnormal. A common culprit is the mechanical brake switch being out of adjustment or failing.

Because the brake switch is safety-relevant, the PCM may disable cruise until the fault is fixed.
safetyImpact: Cruise disabled; brake lights may misbehave.

faq.a: Often no — brake lights must function.

title: Cruise Control / Brake Switch A Circuit Low Advanced
shortDescription: Brake switch A circuit low.
fullDescription: P0572 sets when the brake switch A circuit reads low constantly, suggesting a short to ground or stuck-closed switch.
safetyImpact: Possible cruise fault and brake light issue.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm short clears with switch unplugged.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Trace for pinched or chafed wires.

faq.a: Safety logic won't allow cruise with bad brake input.

title: Cruise Control / Brake Switch A Circuit High Advanced
shortDescription: Brake switch A circuit high.
fullDescription: P0573 sets when the PCM reads constant high on the switch A input, implying open or stuck-open switch.
safetyImpact: Brake lights may not function; cruise disabled.

faq.a: Only if brake lights fail — not safe otherwise.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
shortDescription: Multi-function cruise input A reading low.
fullDescription: P0580 sets with low input voltage on the multiplexed cruise switch input. Often due to a shorted ladder resistor or shorted button contact.

fixSteps.title: Measure input
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at PCM input pin.

faq.a: Possibly; check continuity.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
shortDescription: Multi-function cruise input A reading high.
fullDescription: P0581 sets when input voltage is above threshold. Usually due to open wiring or an open switch.

fixSteps.title: Continuity check
fixSteps.instruction: Trace the input wire to the PCM.

faq.a: Yes, cruise just offline.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Stuck
shortDescription: Cruise multi-function input B appears stuck.
fullDescription: P0590 sets when the PCM sees input B fixed at one value, implying a stuck button. Frequent cause: water intrusion in steering wheel controls.

fixSteps.title: Press all buttons
fixSteps.instruction: Verify each button toggles the input.

faq.a: Clear DTC after repair.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Cruise input B out of range.
fullDescription: P0591 sets when input B produces values outside the calibrated ladder. A drifted resistor or poor contact is suspected.

fixSteps.title: Measure ladder
fixSteps.instruction: Check each button's resistance per spec.

faq.a: Usually not — separate circuit.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Cruise input B reading low.
fullDescription: P0592 sets when input B voltage remains low. Typical short-to-ground fault.

faq.a: No — PCM needs valid input.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High
shortDescription: Cruise input B reading high.
fullDescription: P0593 sets when input B voltage remains high, indicating an open connection or disconnected plug.

faq.a: Generally 1 hour or less.

title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Open
shortDescription: Cruise servo control circuit is open.
fullDescription: P0594 applies to vehicles with a mechanical cruise servo. The PCM cannot command the servo due to open wiring or failed servo motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure servo cable to throttle is intact.

faq.a: No — this is for mechanical cable cruise.

title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Short
shortDescription: Servo control circuit shorted.
fullDescription: P0595 sets when a short is detected in the cruise servo control wire. The PCM disables cruise to prevent damage.

faq.a: Yes.

title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range
shortDescription: Servo response outside calibrated range.
fullDescription: P0596 sets when servo position feedback diverges from command. A binding cable or weak vacuum supply are common culprits on vacuum servos.

faq.a: On diesels, possibly.

title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Open
shortDescription: Thermostat heater control circuit open.
fullDescription: P0597 applies to engines with electrically heated thermostats. Code sets when PCM cannot drive the heater due to an open circuit.

faq.a: No — only a heater fault.

title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Thermostat heater circuit shorted low.
fullDescription: P0598 appears when the control wire shorts to ground. The heater may be stuck on.

faq.a: Yes, limited impact.

title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Thermostat heater circuit reads high.
fullDescription: P0599 sets with elevated voltage on the control wire, usually an open or unplugged thermostat.

faq.a: Improves emissions during warm-up.

title: Serial Communication Link Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnosis of serial link fault between modules.
fullDescription:
P0600 is a generic serial communication fault. The PCM or a related module cannot communicate reliably over the CAN or other serial bus.

Lost communication can stem from a bad terminating resistor, broken bus wire, failed module, or noisy ground.

The advanced approach uses a scope to visualize waveform integrity.
safetyImpact: Potential loss of multiple systems; limp mode likely.

fixSteps.title: Scope CAN
fixSteps.instruction: Visualize CAN H and L waveforms.

fixSteps.title: Bus resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Ign off, measure ~60 ohms across CAN.

fixSteps.title: Isolate module
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect modules one by one to find culprit.

faq.a: Sometimes; often another module on the bus.

title: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for shift solenoid A.
fullDescription:
P0750 sets when the TCM/PCM sees a functional problem with shift solenoid A. The advanced path captures pressure response timing and electrical signature simultaneously.

Causes range from clogged hydraulic passages, worn valve body, to a failing solenoid coil. Dirty fluid commonly masks the root cause.

fixSteps.title: Fluid service
fixSteps.instruction: Drop pan, inspect filter and magnet.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new solenoid or valve body.

faq.a: Sometimes; worth trying first.

title: Shift Solenoid B Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for shift solenoid B.
fullDescription: Analogous to P0750 but affecting the B solenoid. Solenoid B typically controls a different shift pair, so symptoms vary with the transmission design.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new solenoid if out of spec.

faq.a: Not necessarily — many are solenoid-only.

title: Shift Solenoid C Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for shift solenoid C.
fullDescription: P0760 covers solenoid C issues. Diagnostic steps are similar to other shift solenoids; advanced path uses pressure testing in addition to electrical checks.

faq.a: Short distances, gently.

title: Shift Solenoid D Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for shift solenoid D.
fullDescription: P0765 addresses solenoid D faults. This solenoid often controls overdrive in many units. Advanced diagnosis includes pressure tap testing to confirm hydraulic response.

fixSteps.title: Data capture
fixSteps.instruction: Log commanded vs actual gear at highway speed.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new solenoid or valve body.

faq.a: Likely lost overdrive.

title: Shift Solenoid E Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for shift solenoid E.
fullDescription: Code P0770 addresses solenoid E issues, often the TCC solenoid or a line pressure control on some units. Diagnosis is identical to other solenoid codes.
safetyImpact: TCC may not lock; heat buildup possible.

faq.q: Why does engine die at stops?
faq.a: TCC stuck on won't allow torque converter to release.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Advanced
shortDescription: Pressure control solenoid B abnormal.
fullDescription:
P0775 indicates the pressure control solenoid B is not responding correctly. Advanced diagnosis includes live pressure tap.

Pressure control solenoids frequently wear due to internal debris.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test
fixSteps.instruction: Tap line pressure and compare to spec.

faq.a: Not always — solenoid swap often fixes.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance Advanced
shortDescription: Pressure control solenoid B performance fault.
fullDescription: P0776 appears when the B solenoid electrically passes but hydraulic response is sluggish. Debris in the valve body or worn bores are typical.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to spec at idle and stall.

faq.a: Not recommended; address mechanically.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On Advanced
shortDescription: Pressure control solenoid B stuck on.
fullDescription: P0777 sets when solenoid B response suggests it's stuck fully open, causing line pressure issues and potential harsh engagement.

faq.a: Trailer preferred; internal damage risk.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical Advanced
shortDescription: Electrical fault in pressure control solenoid B.
fullDescription: P0778 points to an electrical issue in solenoid B — typically open or shorted coil.

faq.a: Often; internal TCM connector can corrode.

title: Shift Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: General shift malfunction detected.
fullDescription: P0780 sets when the TCM cannot command a shift that completes correctly. The root cause can be hydraulic, mechanical, or electrical.

fixSteps.title: Specialist diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Refer to transmission specialist if needed.

faq.a: Not always — start with fluid and scan data.

title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
shortDescription: Transfer case controller requesting MIL illumination.
fullDescription: P0800 indicates the transfer case control module has detected a fault and is requesting the MIL be illuminated. Scan the TCCM directly for specific sub-codes.

fixSteps.title: Read TCCM codes
fixSteps.instruction: Connect scanner to transfer case module.

faq.a: Usually yes.

title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
shortDescription: Reverse inhibit control circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: P0801 sets when the reverse inhibit circuit used by the transfer case/PTO is faulty. Typical on manual-transmission PTO setups.

faq.a: Yes, on many trucks.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Clutch pedal position sensor out of spec.
fullDescription: P0805 sets when clutch pedal position sensor readings don't correlate with pedal movement. Applies to manual transmissions and dual-clutch systems.
safetyImpact: Start-in-gear inhibit may be disabled; DSG may behave oddly.

fixSteps.title: Data check
fixSteps.instruction: Watch pedal position in scan tool.

faq.a: Yes, but starting in gear may be blocked.

title: Clutch Position Control Error
shortDescription: Clutch actuator not reaching commanded position.
fullDescription: P0810 sets when a clutch actuator (DCT/AMT) cannot achieve the commanded position within tolerance. Could indicate worn clutch, low hydraulic pressure, or actuator failure.

fixSteps.title: Actuator diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory scan tool for clutch adaptations.

faq.a: Often yes on DCT-equipped vehicles.

title: Upshift Switch Circuit
shortDescription: Upshift switch circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: P0815 indicates the upshift switch circuit (paddle or gearshift) is faulty. Commonly on automatic manual shifters.

faq.a: Yes — usually only manual mode affected.

title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Gear lever X-Y position sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0820 sets on shifters that use X-Y position sensors. A fault leaves the PCM unsure of shifter position and may inhibit engine start or gear engagement.

fixSteps.title: Replace shifter
fixSteps.instruction: Install new assembly if sensor integrated.

faq.a: If it runs, yes — watch gear display carefully.
